items.headline: Trump rules out new Iran strikes before the midterms — oil eases, diplomacy window opens
bullets: Numbers: Trump wrote on Truth Social (Oct 8) the US will not be "attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections" (Nov 3), citing "productive discussions" with Iran; the blockade "will remain in full force and effect." Brent fell 0.7% to $103.53 and WTI 0.6% to $90.97 early Friday after spiking ~4% Thursday. Iran's Tasnim reported Tehran is reviewing a US response to its proposal to reopen Hormuz within 7 days. The US imposed fresh sanctions Thursday on Iranian crude networks and 17 vessels.

Meaning: escalation with a ceiling — Washington takes a pre-election strike off the table and points to a diplomacy track while keeping the economic blockade. That's a de-escalation signal, not a deal: Iran hasn't confirmed the talks, Thursday's Houthi strikes on Riyadh airports already happened, and oil gave back only ~$2 of the strike-fear premium. A confirmed Hormuz reopening would unwind much more.

FX: USD near 18-month highs (DXY ~102.2, 10Y ~5.30%) with the war premium still embedded; de-escalation leans mild risk-on — AUD +0.3% to $0.6974, USD/JPY ~157.9 steady as the haven bid softens but the wide yield gap caps yen strength; CAD cushioned by $103 oil; EUR near 17-month lows (~$1.12) as the energy-cost drag lingers. If Tehran confirms the talks track, expect further haven unwind (JPY/CHF softer, AUD/NZD firmer).

items.headline: Houthi missiles hit Riyadh airport — third straight day of strikes on Saudi aviation
bullets: Numbers: Houthi ballistic/cruise missiles struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday — third straight day of attacks on Saudi airports. 3 killed and 36 wounded over two days at Riyadh + Abha airports (Saudi GACA). An empty commercial aircraft was hit at Terminal 4; dozens of incoming flights canceled or diverted. Saudi intercepted two ballistic missiles over Riyadh; falling debris damaged a kindergarten and medical clinic. Brent settled Thursday at $104.28 (+4%), easing to ~$103.5 early Friday after Trump ruled out US strikes before the Nov 3 midterms.

Meaning: escalation-with-a-ceiling — Iran's Houthi allies are retaliating asymmetrically for the Saudi-led Yemen offensive and the US blockade, widening the conflict from shipping to civil aviation in the capital. Risk premium is spreading from shipping to air travel. Trump ruling out US strikes before the midterms caps the tail, but the two-way pressure keeps a supply-shock premium in oil.

FX: USD near 18-month highs (DXY ~102.3, US 10Y ~5.30%) on risk-off flows and inflation repricing; JPY/CHF supported by haven flows; USD/JPY ~157.9–158.1 held steady as haven bid meets the wide yield gap (intervention watch); AUD/NZD soft on risk-off; CAD cushioned by $103 oil; EUR pinned near $1.121 on the energy-cost drag.

bullets: Numbers: Brent spiked 5.7% intraday to $105.91, WTI to $93.20, on reports the White House asked the Pentagon for limited Iran strike options; both faded by midday (Brent $103.63, WTI $90.87). Nine tankers attacked in/around the Strait of Hormuz this week — most since the war began Feb 28. Reuters reported US strikes Wednesday on an Iranian drone-control site near Bandar Abbas.

Meaning: fresh supply-shock premium layered onto a tight oil market; Trump then ruled out new strikes before the Nov 3 midterms, helping oil give back ~$2. IEA agreed to accelerate release of 100M barrels from emergency stocks. Markets price escalation-with-a-ceiling: tail risk up, no open-ended strike path yet.

FX: CAD bid via terms of trade (loonie led G10 intraday); USD bid near 18-month highs on risk-off flows and inflation repricing (DXY ~102.2–102.4, US 10Y ~5.35%); EUR pinned near 17-month lows (~$1.12) on the energy-cost drag; JPY supported by haven flows but capped by wide yield differentials (USD/JPY ~158.2)
